task.title: Validate portable relative extension entrypoints
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/598 by rejecting host-absolute, traversal-shaped, and non-portable entrypoint metadata before filesystem lookup.
acceptance_criteria: Accept one or more normal forward-slash relative path components and preserve the authored value.
Reject absolute, empty, dot, parent, backslash, control-character, and platform-reserved forms.
Return one deterministic typed entrypoint error without inspecting the filesystem.
Document that lexical validation is not an activation or filesystem sandbox.

attempts.summary: Established RED for portable entrypoint metadata.
attempts.diagnostic: The manifest loader accepted every non-blank entrypoint, including absolute paths, parent traversal, backslashes, reserved names, and malformed components.
attempts.patch: Added table-driven accepted and rejected path tests covering Unix, Windows, control-character, and component-boundary cases.

attempts.diagnostic: A platform-independent component validator rejects unsafe metadata early while deferring actual containment and file-type checks to discovery or loading.
attempts.patch: Added validate_entrypoint, InvalidEntrypoint, Windows-reserved component checks, documentation, and milestone evidence without filesystem access.

attempts.summary: Verified and merged the lexical boundary.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused tests, full pinned verification, exact-head CI, substantive review, and unresolved-thread checks all passed.
attempts.patch: Pull request 599 squash-merged as d4a00664d18095bb34d8d125997cc15c1ea56350 and closed issue 598.

outcome.summary: Version-one manifests now preserve valid portable relative entrypoints and reject unsafe or platform-specific path shapes before discovery or activation.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30172736071 and substantive CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/599

lessons: Portable lexical validation should happen before platform filesystem semantics can diverge.
Relative syntax alone does not prove containment; descriptor-anchored target validation remains necessary.
Preserving valid authored values keeps metadata identity separate from validation policy.
One typed public error can keep the boundary stable while tests cover detailed rejection shapes.
